$comment: Kiln's install for this frame, as data. `device`: what Kiln's device flows read (kiln-core DeviceFrame): its names, board, release line, timings, assets, the browser storage it keeps, and its words. Format: docs/design/kiln/frames-as-data.md. A draft (#621): the contract (kiln/apps/kiln/test/contract) reads route, touch and each step's id, writes, reboots, downloads and taps; the engine reads the rest from phase 2.

enter.why: VOL- is on a board inside the case. On the Glass Panes image the Mirror runs adb, so phase 2 enters fastboot with adb reboot bootloader.

connect.title: Connect to your Mirror
connect.body: Plug it into this computer over micro-USB, with Glassworks running.

listed.why: The name Chrome's USB list shows the Mirror by, over adb and in fastboot alike: nobody finds "the Mirror" there (maintainer, 2026-11-21). Kiln's screens say it wherever they ask for a pick, and set-up's sheet names it

apk.why: Glassworks' legacy build, for Android 6; its CPU runs 64-bit apps (frame.json abis)

timings.why: authMs: how long the keep step waits for the Mirror to let this browser's adb key in (a Mirror that trusts another browser's key waits for a tap it can't take); firstStartAuthMs: the first start's first try, longer since a Mirror that just restarted takes its time (PR 607); readMs: one read over adb

assets.why: branding/lululemon-mirror/bootanimation.zip and frames/lululemon-mirror/overlay/GlassworksSettings.apk (Wi-Fi on, no screen timeout, no lock screen, no auto-rotate), staged with Kiln's other assets

storage.why: localStorage: this browser has flashed a Mirror (issue 580). Browsers hold it: never rename

words.image.vendor: Its vendor files are Qualcomm's and Quectel's, from the Glass Panes release.
words.image.lede: Kiln adds Glassworks to the Glass Panes image and writes it over USB.
words.fastboot.restarted: The Mirror is restarting into fastboot. Click Connect and pick `Android`.
words.fastboot.byHandSteps:
Switch the Mirror off with the rocker switch in its bottom edge, unplug its power cord, and lay it face down.
Take out the 4 screws in the bottom edge and take the stand off. Take out the 14 screws in the back, 2 of them either side of the recess by the feet, and lift the back off.
Plug the power cord back into its socket in that recess. Leave the switch off.
Plug the micro-USB port, in the top end's corner, into this computer.
On the small green board at the top end, hold VOL− (SW3): of its two buttons, the one nearer the top end's edge.
Keep holding while you switch the Mirror on, and for about 5 seconds more. Its screen stays black.
words.fastboot.byHandNote: Hold only VOL−: both buttons, or VOL+, start other modes. Some Mirrors have a service hatch in the back that reaches the board.
words.fastboot.overUsb: It already runs Glassworks (or Glass Panes): restart it over USB
words.confirm.title: This replaces lululemon’s software for good
words.confirm.lede: Everything on the Mirror is replaced, with no backup: its bootloader can't read anything back. The way back is the plain Glass Panes image.
words.confirm.understand: I understand lululemon's software can't be restored.
words.adb.firstStart: Its glass stays dark for a few minutes. Leave it plugged in, click Connect and pick `Android`.
words.done.noTouch: The Mirror has no touchscreen: hide the other launcher again, or use a USB mouse to choose Glassworks, then Always.
words.done.noHomeFix: Add a build of Glassworks made for Android 6, over adb.
words.error.noFill: If the bootloader refused a FILL chunk, try again without FILL. It sends about 200 MB more.
words.keep.steps: Plug the Mirror's micro-USB into this computer, with Glassworks running.
words.community.ifVendor: If it still has lululemon's software, that can't be restored, by Kiln or anyone.
words.app.pick.release: Kiln installs Glassworks' newest release over USB and makes it the Mirror's only home screen.
words.app.pick.local: Pick the legacy build of Glassworks for generic Android. Kiln makes it the Mirror's only home screen.
words.app.connectHelp: Plug the Mirror into this computer, click Connect and pick it. Then choose **Allow** on the Mirror, with a USB mouse.
words.fastboot.notLetIn: The Mirror didn't let this browser in: it runs lululemon's software, or Glassworks from another browser. Put it in fastboot with the steps above.

on.line: Updates from Home Assistant install by themselves.

normal-app.line: Android asks before each update, and the Mirror has no touchscreen to answer: use a USB mouse. An install over fastboot makes updates silent.

not-granted.line: Android didn't let Glassworks install its own updates, so each one asks first. Write the image again to fix it.

unknown.line: Kiln couldn't read it back. Glassworks' Device page on the Mirror says.

install.text: Copy the APK to the Mirror
Android installs it and optimises it
First start, with your Home Assistant
Make it the only home screen
